# Carbon dioxide's lines (M65): HITRAN's 470,000 lines from 400 to 6,500 cm^-1 of its four
# commonest isotopologues, 626, 636, 628 and 627, their intensities carrying their natural
# abundances (Gordon et al. 2022, HITRAN2020, hitran.org/lbl, downloaded 2026-11-11). Each line
# a Lorentz profile air-broadened at 500 hPa, the 15 um band's reference pressure, times its
# chi factor, sub-Lorentzian beyond 3 cm^-1 of its centre (Perrin and Hartmann 1989, refitted
# for pure carbon dioxide by band, nu2's to 1800 cm^-1, nu3's to 3200 and past 4300, nu1+nu3's
# between, from 200 to 770 K: Chaverot et al. 2025, A&A, Tables 1 to 3); its strength at each
# temperature by its lower state's energy, the stimulated emission and the partition function
# (rotation as T, the harmonic vibrations 1333, 2 x 667 and 2349 cm^-1). On each of the model's
# spectral bins: the lines within 25 cm^-1 of their centres, from 950 cm^-1 (below it the 15 um
# band's fit, CO2_BAND), their spectrum's median (Williams 2026's way) and its mean, the lines'
# strength spread evenly over the bin, which a bin's lines broadened into each other absorb at
# most; and from 400 cm^-1 the far wings of the lines a millionth as strong as the strongest or
# more, from 25 to 1,500 cm^-1 of their centres, their mean over the bin.
#
# T t_1 t_2 ... (K)
# upper edge (cm^-1), then median, mean and wings at each temperature (m^2/kg at 500 hPa)
from 400
T 150 250 400 700
